evidence_description: Camp managers should prepare a camp management plan in consultation with affected communities for all flying-fox camp management actions. Some high impact and high-risk actions under the Code will require the development of a camp management plan. Camp management action at nationally important flying-fox camps may require referral to the Australian Government under the EPBC Act. NSW DCCEEW states understorey weeds can provide important roosting habitat for flying-foxes, especially in heat stress events.

source_authority: Sam Horton, Senior Policy Officer, Species Listing, Information and Policy Section, Protected Species and Ecological Communities Branch, Biodiversity Division, Commonwealth Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
source_title: DCCEEW reply confirming the National Flying Fox Monitoring Program has been paused since 2022
hash_exception_reason: Not this case's own original evidence. This is the operator's real email exchange with DCCEEW about the Bellbrook camp (this repository's own adjacent case, DFAPTI-BB-FF-2026-00001, EV-0022/EV-0023), pasted into conversation on 2026-08-23. Added here because its content is generic to the National Flying Fox Monitoring Program's operating status, not specific to the Bellbrook site, and bears directly on this case's own camp-registration remedy demands.
evidence_description: DCCEEW's reply to the operator's own 18 June 2026 registration notification for the Bellbrook camp. States the National Flying Fox Monitoring Program (NFFMP) - a collaboration between national, state/territory governments, CSIRO, local governments and community volunteers - was PAUSED in 2022 due to cessation of federal funding, to allow participating partners to consider future investment approaches. States the Department is not currently monitoring flying-fox camps under the NFFMP and cannot send resources to survey a camp. States grey-headed flying-foxes remain federally protected and any camp exceeding the 'nationally important camp' threshold would still need referral. Recommends engaging the relevant state government instead.
relevant_quotation: The NFFMP was paused in 2022 due to a cessation of federal funding... As the NFFMP is not currently monitoring flying-fox camps, the department is unable to send out resources to survey the camp.
investigation_relevance: This case's own remedy demands (NVC-2, NSW-1/NSW-2/NSW-3, CWLTH-1/CWLTH-2, DNSW-2), Lattice Atlas Emergent Pattern 3 (the Grant Eligibility Lock, described as the case's single most actionable finding), and Temporal Projection Integrity Engine assessments TPA-002/TPA-003/TPA-005 all treat notifying the camp to the National Flying-Fox Monitoring Program as a live, near-term action available to anyone. This reply - obtained by the operator directly attempting exactly that action for a comparable NSW hinterland camp - shows the Commonwealth program itself has had no operating capacity since 2022, independent of anything Nambucca Valley Council has or hasn't done. See CTR-0003.
